need_summary: Around 1.2 million people in England are on a COPD register, with high rates of unplanned admissions and post-discharge readmission. Many high-risk patients lack structured remote monitoring or dependable self-management support between appointments.
pathway_gap: Discharge bundles are often missed or paper-based; pulmonary rehabilitation capacity is limited; and clinical teams lack early warning when symptoms worsen at home.
why_addressable: NICE early value assessment recommends clinically assured digital therapeutics for COPD self-management and remote monitoring during evidence generation. A digital layer can systematise discharge support, extend PR reach, and enable proactive monitoring with clinical escalation.
intervention_types: Remote monitoring with clinical hub (high-risk cohort)

impact_headline.metric: Emergency respiratory admissions avoided (remote monitoring, 500-patient cohort)
impact_headline.source: Bradford 786-patient evaluation; corroborated Sunderland and Frimley

impact_headline.metric: Net economic value (ICB combined pathway, per year)
impact_headline.source: HealthStore DTx business case model v5 (illustrative)

commissioning_considerations: Identify clinical owner for remote monitoring hub and discharge self-management
Confirm acute provider tariff gateway position for COPD best practice bundle
Complete local DCB0160 clinical safety and IG assessment
Agree evaluation and data-return obligations with supplier
Fund monitoring from ICB baselines; consider central licence funding for self-management
